name: Ferrari 512 S
description:
The Ferrari 512 S is a Group 5 sports prototype built by Ferrari to compete against the dominant Porsche 917 in the 1970 World Sportscar Championship. The "512" designation refers to its 5-liter, 12-cylinder engine configuration, while "S" stands for Sport.

Developed in just three months under the direction of legendary engineer Mauro Forghieri, the 512 S was Ferrari's urgent response to the FIA's new 5-liter regulations. The car featured an all-aluminum 4,993cc V12 engine with four valves per cylinder, producing 550 horsepower at 8,500 RPM. Its tubular spaceframe chassis evolved from Ferrari's successful P4 and 612 Can-Am designs, while Giacomo Caliri penned the striking bodywork, constructed from lightweight polycarbonate.

Available in both berlinetta (coupe) and spider configurations, the 512 S became an icon of endurance racing. The car achieved notable victories at Sebring and Kyalami during the 1970-1971 seasons, and famously starred alongside the Porsche 917 in Steve McQueen's 1971 film "Le Mans." Though ultimately overshadowed by the Porsche in period competition, the 512 S remains one of Ferrari's most beautiful and evocative racing machines, embodying the raw drama of early 1970s prototype racing.
